blocks.text: JUDGE OF ISRAEL · THE TRIBES OF ISRAEL
Samson. A Nazarite who judged Israel twenty years "in the days of the Philistines".
LED ISRAELi
20 years No years BC in Scripture
TRIBE
Dan
IN THE LINE
13th of 15
SCRIPTURE SAYS
“The child shall be a Nazarite unto God from the womb: and he shall begin to deliver Israel out of the hand…”
PROPHETS
None named
THE TRIBES OF ISRAEL: 15 RULERS MOSES → SAMUEL
THE CYCLE
Forgetting, oppression, a cry, a deliverer, rest
1 · FORGOT GOD "The children of Israel did evil again in the sight of the LORD." Judges 13:1
2 · OPPRESSED: THE PHILISTINES, 40 YEARS "The LORD delivered them into the hand of the Philistines forty years." Judges 13:1
3 · CRIED OUT Scripture does not say.
4 · DELIVERED He was to "begin to deliver Israel"; he fought the Philistines alone, and at his death killed their lords in Dagon's house. Judges 13:5 Judges 16:30
5 · REST Scripture does not say.
ACCESSION
How Samson came to power
The angel of the LORD told Manoah's barren wife she would bear a son who must be a Nazarite. Judges 13:2–5
Manoah offered a kid, and the angel ascended in the flame of the altar. Judges 13:19–20
"The woman bare a son, and called his name Samson"; the Spirit began to move him between Zorah and Eshtaol. Judges 13:24–25
SUCCESSION
Before and after
WHAT SCRIPTURE SAYS
What Scripture says of him
"The child shall be a Nazarite unto God from the womb: and he shall begin to deliver Israel out of the hand of the Philistines." Judges 13:5
The Spirit of the LORD came upon him again and again. Judges 13:25 Judges 14:6 Judges 14:19 Judges 15:14
His marriage at Timnath "was of the LORD, that he sought an occasion against the Philistines". Judges 14:4
When he was shaven, "he wist not that the LORD was departed from him". Judges 16:20
"The dead which he slew at his death were more than they which he slew in his life." Judges 16:30
Hebrews names him among those who acted by faith. Hebrews 11:32
EVENTS
Wars, works and turning points
UNDATED IN SCRIPTURE
THE LAND
The places Scripture names
The tribes of Israel · tribe of Dan. Only places Scripture names are shown, each where the Atlas puts it.
THE NATION
What the nation did
The Philistines held a great sacrifice to Dagon, saying "Our god hath delivered Samson our enemy into our hand". Judges 16:23–24
ON THE WORLD STAGE
The powers of the day
THE PHILISTINES
The lords of the Philistines (not named)
DATES DIFFER
When was it?
SCRIPTURE'S OWN NUMBERS
No years given
Twenty years of judging inside, or after, the forty years of Philistine rule (Judges 13:1, 15:20, 16:31); see the open question.
Yes, inside the forty
Keil (1865); Moore's scheme (1895)

Keil reads "in the days of the Philistines" as "during the oppression of the Philistines", so Samson's years are not added separately; Moore's scheme also counts the forty as Samson's twenty and Eli's twenty.[1][19]
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 5
Judges 13 Judges 14 Judges 15 Judges 16 Hebrews 11
PASSAGES · 2
Judges 13:1–16:31 Hebrews 11:32
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Unlike the earlier cycles, no cry to the LORD is recorded before Samson (Judges 13:1-2).
Samson never leads an Israelite army; he fights alone.
Judges does not record the end of the Philistines' forty years; the Philistines are subdued in Samuel's time (1 Samuel 7:13).
